# pheno-axum-stack

Pre-wired Axum router for pheno services. Composes
`pheno-tower::Service` + `pheno-tokio-base::shutdown_signal` +
`pheno-tracing` into a single `app()` function that returns a fully
middleware-wired `axum::Router` with CORS, request-id, trace-context,
health check, and 404 fallback.

## Install

```toml
[dependencies]
pheno-axum-stack = { path = "../pheno-axum-stack" }
axum = "0.7"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }
pheno-tokio-base = { path = "../pheno-tokio-base" }
```

## Public API

```rust
pub fn app() -> axum::Router;          // canonical pre-wired router
pub fn health_router() -> axum::Router; // /healthz + 404 only
```

## Usage

```rust
use pheno_axum_stack::app;
use pheno_tokio_base::{runtime, shutdown_signal};

fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let rt = runtime();
    rt.block_on(async {
        let app = app().route("/", axum::routing::get(|| async { "hello" }));
        let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("0.0.0.0:8080").await?;
        axum::serve(listener, app)
            .with_graceful_shutdown(shutdown_signal())
            .await
    })
}
```

## Middleware stack

1. TraceLayer (outermost)
2. RequestIdLayer
3. CorsLayer (default permissive)
4. CatchPanicLayer
5. (your routes)

## Scope-out

- Not an Axum replacement. Use `axum` types directly.
- No OpenAPI generator. Use `utoipa` or `aide` if needed.
- No database layer. Use `sqlx` or `sea-orm` directly.

## Tests

2/2 unit tests pass. Test commands: `cargo test -p pheno-axum-stack`.
